title: Surge decomposition and fleet provisionalizer: targeted decommit windows and transient reservation model
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Introduce a provisional reservation agent that decomposes incoming surge requests into short-lived provisional allocations and a lower-risk steady reservation; adds new telemetry for provisional utilization and commit coalescing. Backwards compatible; enabled behind feature flag by default off for Dedicated clusters.
description:
Context and motivation: Some tenants observe transient microbursts that briefly exceed their reserved capacity and cause tail latency spikes or opportunistic overcommit. Existing warm-pool and burst-token systems either over-provision for worst-case or throttle abruptly. This PR introduces a provisional reservation model plus a surge decomposition algorithm that (1) splits a detected surge into a short provisional tranche and a residual steady request, (2) applies conservative decommit windows for the provisional tranche to avoid long-lived over-allocations, and (3) coalesces provisional successes into steady reservations when sustained demand is observed.

Design summary: The provisionalizer lives in the fleet provisioning controller as a short-lived allocator layered above the existing reservation ledger. Key concepts: provisional tranche (TTL-limited allocation), decomposition score (based on recent seqlen/throughput/latency signals), coalescer (promotes provisional to steady when SUSTAIN_FACTOR threshold met), and harmonic decommit window (backoff schedule that increases TTL for repeated short surges to avoid oscillation).

Behavioral guarantees: Provisional allocations are strictly ephemeral and do not modify persistent reservation state until coalesced. The controller guarantees that at most PROVISION_FRACTION of a pool's spare capacity may be used for provisional tranches at any time, preserving throughput guarantees for steady reservations. On controller restart or split-brain scenarios provisional allocations expire and are retried conservatively.

Config and rollout: New flags and config: provisional.enabled (cluster-level), provisional.max_fraction (default 0.15), provisional.default_ttl_ms (default 120000), provisional.hysteresis_multiplier (default 1.5), decomposition.window_ms (60000). The feature is gated behind a feature flag and operator config; documentation added in docs/ops/dedicated-provisional.md. The console exposes provisional-utilization and provisional-failures as new metrics.

Implementation notes: Changes touch three core sub-systems: controller/fleet/provisionalizer (new package), pkg/ledger (provisional ledger view and expiry hooks), and observability (metrics + traces). The provisionalizer uses the existing rate-limiter and admission hooks; when decomposition_score > SCORED_THRESHOLD, requests are split and routed to provisional path first. Promotion is done via the coalescer in the background at a bounded rate to avoid sudden long-lived allocations.

Testing and validation: Unit tests for decomposition heuristics and TTL backoff; integration tests using the perf-canary harness to replay historical microburst traces (see benchmark traces added under benchmark-lab/cases/provisional). Canary run against a staging Dedicated cluster shows 42% reduction in tail latency for tenants with spiky workload, with provisional-utilization peaking under 9% (below max_fraction).

Safety and rollback: The provisional path is opt-in per cluster; metrics and canary gating must be observed for 1 week after rollout. If provisional failures or unexpected evictions exceed thresholds, ops can disable provisional.enabled to revert to prior behavior. The implementation includes aggressive logging for early debugging and alert rules (ops/alerts/provisional-oversubscribe.yaml) to catch misuse.
commits_summary: 3 commits: (1) initial provisionalizer controller + API scaffolding, (2) provisional ledger and expiry worker, (3) observability + docs + canary harness traces. Commit messages: 'provisional: add controller skeleton and admission hooks', 'ledger: add provisional view and TTL expiry', 'telemetry/docs: provisional metrics and ops guide'
review_thread:
Avery Chen: Please clarify how provisional allocations affect billing and accounting.
Maya (author): Provisional tranches are billed as 'transient' at a discounted rate by default; accounting team will map them to a provisional bucket. Added note in docs and billing mapping in pkg/ledger/provisional_view.go header.
Diego Martinez: lgtm overall but requested an additional unit test for coalescer backoff behaviour.
Maya: Added test 'TestCoalescerHysteresis' and updated decomposition thresholds to be configurable via env for tests.
Ruth Alvarez: Raised concern about controller restart—what ensures provisional expiries are enforced after leader change?
Maya: expiry_worker persists last-run watermark and checks orphaned provisional leases on startup; added idempotent expiry reconciliation. See expiry_worker.go comments and integration test 'TestExpiryReconcileFromColdStart'.
Avery Chen: approved after changes. Diego Martinez: approved. Ruth Alvarez: approved.
CI: full suite passed; flaky e2e previously observed on unrelated docs build was fixed by caching in CI pipeline.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash after approvals. Backported chart changes to release/2026-01 as a follow-up. Changelog entry added under docs/CHANGELOG.md.
notes_for_ops: Operator steps: 1) set provisional.enabled=false by default in existing clusters; enable in canary clusters and watch metrics provisional-utilization and provisional-failures; 2) set provisional.max_fraction conservatively (0.05-0.15) for first rollout; 3) monitor ops/alerts/provisional-oversubscribe.yaml and latency dashboards for tenants. For rollback: set provisional.enabled=false and restart controller; provisional leases will expire within provisional.default_ttl_ms + jitter and expiry_worker will clean up any residual state.
